title: Why Doors Delete Your Memory

voices.gary: Laura FGY2WhTYpPnrIDTdsKH5, pitched up with ffmpeg

lines: [urgent] Doors are deleting your memory. And it gets worse.
You march to the kitchen for one thing. One! You step through the door... gone.
[amused] Meet Gary, the tiny intern in your brain. He holds your thought on a sticky note.
Scientists tested it. People forget more walking through a door than walking the same distance with no door.
[panicked] Now add stress. Ten tabs open, phone in your hand, looking for your phone. Gary is on fire.
[warm] Here's the twist. You're not broken. Later research found doors mostly trip you up when your head is already full.
So do one thing at a time, and Gary keeps the note.
[deadpan] Anyway. Why did you walk in here?
sources: Radvansky, Krawietz & Tamplin (2011), Walking through doorways causes forgetting: further explorations, Q J Exp Psychol
McFadyen et al. (2021), Doorways do not always cause forgetting: a multimodal investigation, BMC Psychology, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7938580
